messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Potentially Useful Comparisons
parts:
I see two goals.

One is getting the right questions to the right people
to answer. And maybe keeping track of what needs to be
answered.

A second is tracking answers in a FAQ-like way so that
we don't have to keep answering the same thing again and again
and it's easier for users to find answers.

And we want to make it understandable to the users so
it doesn't just wind up being a monolithic list again.

That's why I was thinking something on the StackOverflow
model might be good. It's almost always a question
we're fielding and what's hard is a way to organize
the answers for reuse.

And I think it makes sense to separate out the interface
issues (install and API) from the Stan modeling issues.
Same for RStanARM and ShinyStan.

- Bob

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Potentially Useful Comparisons
parts:
Bumping this thread.

I think there's an intermediate solution: enable categories on Google Groups.

Google Groups only allows tags or categories, but not both. We are currently using tags.

I propose we switch to using categories. Each thread can only belong to one category at a time. On the board, Bob, Andrew, and I thought we should have this structure:
- modeling
- interfaces
  * CmdStan
  * RStan
  * PyStan
  * Stan.jl
  * StataStan
- rstanarm

Emails directly into the list are not categorized immediately -- someone would have to manually categorize it. We can continue to use emails to reply to threads. I'm not sure if we're going to be able to subscribe to categories, but I'm hopping we can.

Hopefully the users that use the web interface can categorize their own posts. I can categorize a handful a day.

Anyone oppose? Everything will stay the same for us that use email.



Daniel

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Potentially Useful Comparisons
parts:
On Monday, February 8, 2016 at 9:39:13 PM UTC-5, Daniel Lee wrote:
Bumping this thread.

I think there's an intermediate solution: enable categories on Google Groups.

Google Groups only allows tags or categories, but not both. We are currently using tags.
I think tags have not been very helpful, so it wouldn't take much for categories to be better.

I propose we switch to using categories. Each thread can only belong to one category at a time. On the board, Bob, Andrew, and I thought we should have this structure:
- modeling
- interfaces
  * CmdStan
  * RStan
  * PyStan
  * Stan.jl
  * StataStan
- rstanarm

I think "interfaces" is too vague. A lot of people post things like "I have a question about RStan: I am getting this parser error" without realizing they would get the same parser error from any of the interfaces. I would say the top-level category should be "installation" but I don't know if we need to subcategory installation problems by interface. Or maybe by "interfaces" you really mean "interface syntax", in which case subcategorization is probably appropriate but rstanarm would be a distinct interface from rstan in that scheme.
Emails directly into the list are not categorized immediately -- someone would have to manually categorize it.

That was one of the problem with tags. Can categories be made mandatory for new threads?

Ben

On Monday, February 8, 2016 at 10:34:03 PM UTC-5, Daniel Lee wrote:
I'm thinking we should have an overall list with specific "installation" and "rstanarm" sections that are separate. Those are the only two big topics that flood the list that aren't really relevant to other conversations.

We have had a single digit number of rstanarm threads. But I can see questions involving
  1. How do I install $INTERFACE?
  2. What is the syntax for something in $INTERFACE?
  3. I am using $INTERFACE to estimate a model and I don't understand something

The third is often more of a modeling issue or at least one where the answer has relevance regardless of $INTERFACE. I don't see why (2) and (3) go into the same category unless it $INTERFACE == rstanarm.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Potentially Useful Comparisons
parts: Who is making the category rstanarm & shinystan? Those are almost completely unrelated sets of questions and even more unrelated answers.
On Monday, February 8, 2016 at 10:32:14 PM UTC-5, Daniel Lee wrote:
Also, you should have the ability to change things around.
On Mon, Feb 8, 2016 at 10:27 PM, Daniel Lee <bea...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:
rstanarm has its own section. what else are you talking about?
On Mon, Feb 8, 2016 at 10:25 PM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:

On Monday, February 8, 2016 at 9:58:33 PM UTC-5, Daniel Lee wrote:
I think "interfaces" is too vague. A lot of people post things like "I have a question about RStan: I am getting this parser error" without realizing they would get the same parser error from any of the interfaces. I would say the top-level category should be "installation" but I don't know if we need to subcategory installation problems by interface. Or maybe by "interfaces" you really mean "interface syntax", in which case subcategorization is probably appropriate but rstanarm would be a distinct interface from rstan in that scheme.

Sure. We can just have an installation section. 

Where should questions about interface syntax go? Right now, there is no category for them.

Ben
